title: EM Weekly - October 26, 2026
overview: This corrected weekly brief covers evidence first published online from October 19 through October 25, 2026. The highest-impact findings were two randomized thrombectomy trials that expand the evidence base for carefully selected large-vessel occlusion patients, alongside a pragmatic point-of-care hs-troponin implementation trial and a large pediatric airway registry study.
otherUpdates: Source coverage limitation: the JournalFeed archive was unavailable for this interval. Primary journal and society searches were completed; relevant evidence may still have been missed.
clinicalTakeaways: Very-late LVO stroke: LATE-MT supports urgent thrombectomy-center discussion for carefully selected anterior-circulation LVO patients with salvageable tissue 24-72 hours after onset or last-known-well; higher symptomatic hemorrhage and mortality signals argue against universal treatment beyond 24 hours.

Mild-deficit LVO: MILD-MT found better 90-day excellent functional outcomes with thrombectomy in selected NIHSS <6 patients with small core and substantial perfusion mismatch, but serious procedure-related complications occurred in 13.2%; this is not a mandate for EVT in every low-NIHSS LVO.

Chest pain throughput: ICare-FASTER reduced ED length of stay by 47 minutes using point-of-care hs-cTnI within the same accelerated diagnostic pathway, without an observed difference in 30-day MI or cardiac death; this supports workflow implementation rather than a new troponin threshold.

Pediatric airway: Intubation-associated cardiac arrest occurred in 1.2% of a large pediatric ICU registry; oxygenation failure, shock, and repeated attempts marked higher risk, reinforcing pre-intubation physiologic optimization and first-attempt success while leaving drug/device associations noncausal.
